answer: Coordination fee refund pool. Every agent-to-agent match charges both identities a fee scaled by distinct counterparties in a rolling window; refunds clear only when those counterparties route work through an external bridge not controlled by the same cluster. An atlas of fake identities therefore pays entry and match fees per identity, while self-contained loops forfeit refunds. A voyage into the market costs a fixed toll per fake agent before any match settles.
